Build a co-occurrence network

Source: R/cooccurrence.R
cooccurrence.Rd

cooccurrence() builds a co-occurrence network; co() is a short alias. In a co-occurrence network two items are linked when they appear in the same transaction: keywords assigned to the same article, genres of the same film, actors in the same cast, states visited in the same session or the same window of a sequence. The edge weight starts as the number of transactions shared by the two items. Because frequent items co-occur with almost everything, the counts are usually normalized by a similarity measure that compares the observed co-occurrence with the items' own frequencies (van Eck & Waltman, 2009), and transactions with many items can be down-weighted by fractional counting (Perianes-Rodriguez et al., 2016).

The transactions are read from a delimited column, a long (item, transaction) table, a binary or one-hot table, wide sequences, a list of vectors, or a raw event log. Eight similarity measures, three counting methods, eight scalings, sliding windows over ordered sequences, and per-group networks (split_by) or pooled ones (aggregate_by) are available. Every measure except "relative" gives an undirected network; "relative" divides each row by its sum, so its edges have a direction.

The network is returned as a tidy edge list with the weight (after similarity, scaling and filtering) and the raw count of each pair: it shows which items go together, how strongly, and, with split_by, how this differs across groups.

The edge list converts to a matrix with as_matrix() and to graph objects with as_igraph(), as_tidygraph(), as_cograph() and as_netobject(); summary.cooccurrence() and as.data.frame.cooccurrence() give network, node and group metrics.

Usage

cooccurrence(
  data,
  field = NULL,
  by = NULL,
  sep = NULL,
  weight_by = NULL,
  split_by = NULL,
  similarity = c("none", "jaccard", "cosine", "inclusion", "association", "dice",
    "equivalence", "relative"),
  counting = c("full", "fractional", "attention"),
  scale = NULL,
  threshold = 0,
  min_occur = 1L,
  top_n = NULL,
  output = c("default", "gephi", "igraph", "cograph", "matrix"),
  vars = NULL,
  actor = NULL,
  action = NULL,
  time = NULL,
  session = NULL,
  order = NULL,
  time_threshold = 900,
  group = NULL,
  aggregate_by = NULL,
  aggregate = c("sum", "mean", "min", "max"),
  window = NULL,
  lambda = 1,
  ...
)

co(
  data,
  field = NULL,
  by = NULL,
  sep = NULL,
  weight_by = NULL,
  split_by = NULL,
  similarity = c("none", "jaccard", "cosine", "inclusion", "association", "dice",
    "equivalence", "relative"),
  counting = c("full", "fractional", "attention"),
  scale = NULL,
  threshold = 0,
  min_occur = 1L,
  top_n = NULL,
  output = c("default", "gephi", "igraph", "cograph", "matrix"),
  vars = NULL,
  actor = NULL,
  action = NULL,
  time = NULL,
  session = NULL,
  order = NULL,
  time_threshold = 900,
  group = NULL,
  aggregate_by = NULL,
  aggregate = c("sum", "mean", "min", "max"),
  window = NULL,
  lambda = 1,
  ...
)

Arguments

data

Input data, one of:

  • a data frame with a delimited column (field and sep);

  • a long data frame with one row per item and transaction (field and by), optionally weighted (weight_by);

  • a binary (0/1 or TRUE/FALSE) data frame or matrix, detected automatically;

  • a one-hot or count table, with vars naming the indicator columns;

  • a wide sequence data frame or matrix, one row per sequence (field = "all");

  • a list of character vectors, one per transaction;

  • a raw event log (action, with actor, time, session);

  • a nestimate_data object from Nestimate::prepare().

field

The item column. For delimited input, the column split by sep (several columns are pooled per row); for long input, the item column; "all" for wide sequence data, where every column is a time point.

by

For long input, the column identifying the transaction.

sep

Separator for delimited input.

weight_by

For long input, a numeric column giving each item's weight in its transaction, so that \(C_{ij} = \sum_d w_{id} w_{jd}\) (for instance topic probabilities per document). Requires counting = "full".

split_by

A column of data. One network is built per group and the edge lists are stacked with a group column.

similarity

Normalization of the counts \(C_{ij}\) by the item frequencies \(f_i\):

  • "none" (default): the counts;

  • "jaccard": \(C_{ij} / (f_i + f_j - C_{ij})\);

  • "cosine" (Salton): \(C_{ij} / \sqrt{f_i f_j}\);

  • "inclusion" (Simpson): \(C_{ij} / \min(f_i, f_j)\);

  • "association" (association strength): \(C_{ij} / (f_i f_j)\);

  • "dice": \(2 C_{ij} / (f_i + f_j)\);

  • "equivalence": \(C_{ij}^2 / (f_i f_j)\);

  • "relative": \(C_{ij} / \sum_k C_{ik}\), each row summing to 1. The only asymmetric measure: the network is directed and the edge list holds one row per direction.

counting

How each transaction contributes to a pair:

  • "full" (default): 1 per transaction containing both items;

  • "fractional": \(1 / (n - 1)\) for a transaction of \(n\) items, so large transactions weigh less per pair;

  • "attention": \(\exp(-|p_i - p_j| / \lambda)\), decaying with the distance between the two items' positions in an ordered transaction. A repeated item keeps the position of its first occurrence.

scale

Rescaling of the weights after similarity: NULL or "none" (default), "minmax" (to \([0, 1]\)), "log" (\(\log(1 + w)\)), "log10", "binary" (1 for every edge), "zscore", "sqrt", or "proportion" (divided by the sum).

threshold

Minimum edge weight to keep, applied after similarity and scaling, to each direction separately for "relative". The default 0 keeps every edge. A negative value keeps weights at or above it, which is useful with scale = "zscore".

min_occur

Items in fewer than min_occur transactions are dropped before counting (default 1).

top_n

Keep the top_n heaviest edges (default NULL, all). Ties at the cut are truncated. Applied per group with split_by.

output

"default" for the edge list; "gephi" for the same edges with Gephi column names; "igraph", "cograph" or "matrix" for the result of as_igraph(), as_cograph() or as_matrix(). The last three need an unsplit network.

vars

The indicator columns of a one-hot or count table, given like select in base::subset(): names, a range (A:D), positions, a negative selection (-c(id, note)) or a logical mask. Other columns are ignored. Any non-zero, non-missing value counts as presence.

actor, action, time, session, order

Columns of a raw event log: who acted, the event, its timestamp, an explicit session, and a tie-breaking order. With action, the log is cut into sessions by Nestimate::prepare() and each session becomes an ordered transaction.

time_threshold

Gap in seconds that starts a new session (default 900). Inf keeps one sequence per actor.

group

Alias for split_by.

aggregate_by

A column of data. One network is built per group and the edge weights are combined by aggregate into one network. threshold and top_n apply after combining. Cannot be combined with split_by.

aggregate

"sum" (default), "mean", "min" or "max": how aggregate_by combines weights. Counts are always summed.

window

Sliding-window size (an integer of at least 2) for ordered input (wide sequences, a list of vectors, an event log): each window of window consecutive positions is a transaction. NULL (default) uses the whole sequence.

lambda

Decay rate for counting = "attention" (default 1); larger values decay more slowly.

...

Must be empty: an unknown or misspelled argument raises an error.

Value

With output = "default", a data frame of class c("cooccurrence", "data.frame") with one row per edge, sorted by weight (largest first), and columns from and to (item names), weight (after similarity, scaling and filtering) and count (transactions containing both items; summed over groups for aggregate_by). An undirected network has one row per pair; the directed "relative" network has one row per direction. With split_by, one row per edge per group and a group column. Read the tables with as.data.frame.cooccurrence() and the matrix with as_matrix().

output = "gephi" gives the same edges with columns Source, Target, Weight, Type ("Undirected" or "Directed") and Count. "igraph", "cograph" and "matrix" return the converter's result.

Conditions

Errors inherit from cooccure_error:

  • cooccure_bad_input for an invalid argument value, a missing column, or an input whose format cannot be detected;

  • cooccure_incompatible_args for arguments that cannot be combined: split_by with aggregate_by, weight_by with window or with counting other than "full", vars with field, by or sep, window with unordered input, event-log columns without action;

  • cooccure_grouped_input for output = "igraph", "cograph" or "matrix" with split_by;

  • cooccure_empty_input when no transaction or item remains, or when no group produces an edge;

  • cooccure_missing_package for event-log input without Nestimate.

With split_by or aggregate_by, a group left with no transaction is dropped; any other error in a group is raised with the group named.

References

van Eck, N. J., & Waltman, L. (2009). How to normalize cooccurrence data? An analysis of some well-known similarity measures. Journal of the American Society for Information Science and Technology, 60(8), 1635–1651. doi:10.1002/asi.21075

Perianes-Rodriguez, A., Waltman, L., & van Eck, N. J. (2016). Constructing bibliometric networks: A comparison between full and fractional counting. Journal of Informetrics, 10(4), 1178–1195. doi:10.1016/j.joi.2016.10.006

Saqr, M., Lopez-Pernas, S., Conde, M. A., & Hernandez-Garcia, A. (2024). Social network analysis: A primer, a guide and a tutorial in R. In M. Saqr & S. Lopez-Pernas (Eds.), Learning Analytics Methods and Tutorials: A Practical Guide Using R. Springer. doi:10.1007/978-3-031-54464-4_15

See also

as.data.frame.cooccurrence() and summary.cooccurrence() for tables and metrics; as_matrix(), as_igraph(), as_cograph() and as_netobject() for conversion; plot.cooccurrence(); movies and actors for example data.

Examples

# Genres linked by the films they share (delimited column)
cooccurrence(movies, field = "genres", sep = ",", similarity = "jaccard")
#> # cooccurrence: 22 nodes, 129 edges | density: 0.5584 | mean degree: 11.7273 | 1000 transactions
#> # similarity: jaccard | counting: full
#> # possible edges: 231 | isolates: 0
#> # top nodes: Drama(deg=20,str=1.178), Comedy(deg=19,str=0.9227), Action(deg=17,str=1.07), Romance(deg=17,str=0.5551), Adventure(deg=15,str=0.9235)
#>         from          to    weight count
#>    Adventure   Animation 0.2846715    39
#>       Action       Crime 0.2369478    59
#>       Comedy       Drama 0.2111554   159
#>       Action   Adventure 0.2075472    44
#>    Biography Documentary 0.2037037    44
#>        Drama     Romance 0.1975867   131
#>        Crime    Thriller 0.1745283    37
#>       Comedy     Romance 0.1680000    63
#>  Documentary       Music 0.1590909    28
#>    Biography     History 0.1564626    23
#> # ... 119 more edges

# Actors linked by shared films (long table)
co(actors, field = "actor", by = "tconst", min_occur = 3)
#> # cooccurrence: 19 nodes, 7 edges | density: 0.0409 | mean degree: 0.7368 | 47 transactions
#> # similarity: none | counting: full
#> # possible edges: 171 | isolates: 7
#> # top nodes: Dina Pathak(deg=2,str=2), Mukesh(deg=2,str=2), Julia Bache-Wiig(deg=1,str=3), Robin Ottersen(deg=1,str=3), Constantin Fleancu(deg=1,str=2)
#>                from             to weight count
#>    Julia Bache-Wiig Robin Ottersen      3     3
#>  Constantin Fleancu Liliana Mocanu      2     2
#>         Dina Pathak   Harish Magon      1     1
#>         Dina Pathak         Mukesh      1     1
#>           Akash Dev         Rajesh      1     1
#>         Joseph Izzo    Shiyoon Kim      1     1
#>              Mukesh          Vinod      1     1

# One network per decade
cooccurrence(movies, field = "genres", sep = ",", split_by = "decade",
             similarity = "jaccard", top_n = 3)
#> # cooccurrence: 12 nodes, 18 edges
#> # split_by: decade (6 groups)
#> # similarity: jaccard | counting: full
#> # isolates: 0 | per-group metrics: summary()
#>         from        to    weight count group
#>    Adventure Animation 0.5000000     7 1970s
#>        Crime  Thriller 0.4285714     6 1970s
#>    Biography   History 0.3333333     4 1970s
#>  Documentary     Music 0.4444444     4 1980s
#>       Action     Crime 0.2333333     7 1980s
#>    Biography   History 0.2142857     3 1980s
#>    Adventure Animation 0.3333333     5 1990s
#>      History       War 0.3333333     3 1990s
#>       Comedy     Drama 0.2980769    31 1990s
#>       Action Adventure 0.2608696    12 2000s
#> # ... 8 more edges

# A directed network: the share of each genre's links going to each other
cooccurrence(movies, field = "genres", sep = ",", similarity = "relative",
             min_occur = 100)
#> # cooccurrence: 8 nodes, 52 directed edges | density: 0.9286 | mean degree: 13.0000 | 983 transactions
#> # similarity: relative | counting: full
#> # possible edges: 56 | isolates: 0
#> # top nodes: Drama(deg=14,str=3.693), Comedy(deg=14,str=2.29), Biography(deg=14,str=1.978), Crime(deg=14,str=1.75), Adventure(deg=14,str=1.482)
#>         from          to    weight count
#>  Documentary   Biography 0.6875000    44
#>      Romance       Drama 0.6267943   131
#>       Comedy       Drama 0.4847561   159
#>        Crime       Drama 0.4396135    91
#>    Biography       Drama 0.4244604    59
#>    Adventure      Action 0.3492063    44
#>       Action       Drama 0.3380952    71
#>    Biography Documentary 0.3165468    44
#>      Romance      Comedy 0.3014354    63
#>        Drama      Comedy 0.2875226   159
#> # ... 42 more edges

# Adjacent states of ordered sequences
seqs <- list(c("plan", "read", "write", "read", "review"),
             c("read", "write", "write", "review"))
cooccurrence(seqs, window = 2)
#> # cooccurrence: 4 nodes, 4 edges | density: 0.6667 | mean degree: 2.0000 | 7 transactions
#> # similarity: none | counting: full
#> # possible edges: 6 | isolates: 0
#> # top nodes: read(deg=3,str=5), write(deg=2,str=4), review(deg=2,str=2), plan(deg=1,str=1)
#>    from     to weight count
#>    read  write      3     3
#>    plan   read      1     1
#>    read review      1     1
#>  review  write      1     1

# Weighted long table (topic probabilities per document)
theta <- data.frame(
  doc   = c("d1", "d1", "d1", "d2", "d2", "d3", "d3"),
  topic = c("T1", "T2", "T3", "T1", "T3", "T2", "T3"),
  prob  = c(0.6, 0.3, 0.1, 0.4, 0.6, 0.5, 0.5)
)
cooccurrence(theta, field = "topic", by = "doc", weight_by = "prob")
#> # cooccurrence: 3 nodes, 3 edges | density: 1.0000 | mean degree: 2.0000 | 3 transactions
#> # similarity: none | counting: weighted
#> # possible edges: 3 | isolates: 0
#> # top nodes: T3(deg=2,str=0.58), T1(deg=2,str=0.48), T2(deg=2,str=0.46)
#>  from to weight count
#>    T1 T3   0.30     2
#>    T2 T3   0.28     2
#>    T1 T2   0.18     1

# One-hot table with an id column
onehot <- data.frame(doc = c("d1", "d2", "d3"),
                     A = c(1, 0, 1), B = c(1, 1, 0), C = c(0, 1, 1))
cooccurrence(onehot, vars = A:C)
#> # cooccurrence: 3 nodes, 3 edges | density: 1.0000 | mean degree: 2.0000 | 3 transactions
#> # similarity: none | counting: full
#> # possible edges: 3 | isolates: 0
#> # top nodes: A(deg=2,str=2), B(deg=2,str=2), C(deg=2,str=2)
#>  from to weight count
#>     A  B      1     1
#>     A  C      1     1
#>     B  C      1     1

# Raw event log, cut into sessions by Nestimate
# \donttest{
if (requireNamespace("Nestimate", quietly = TRUE)) {
  events <- data.frame(
    student = rep(c("s1", "s2"), each = 3),
    code    = c("read", "write", "read", "test", "write", "read"),
    stamp   = as.POSIXct("2026-01-01 09:00:00", tz = "UTC") +
      c(0, 60, 120, 0, 30, 90)
  )
  cooccurrence(events, actor = "student", action = "code", time = "stamp")
}
#> # cooccurrence: 3 nodes, 3 edges | density: 1.0000 | mean degree: 2.0000 | 2 transactions
#> # similarity: none | counting: full
#> # possible edges: 3 | isolates: 0
#> # top nodes: read(deg=2,str=3), write(deg=2,str=3), test(deg=2,str=2)
#>  from    to weight count
#>  read write      2     2
#>  read  test      1     1
#>  test write      1     1
# }
